title: KV cache eviction timeline & hypotheses
content:
TL;DR: intermittently seeing token duplication / context bleed after very long requests (> 3k tokens) in hosted tests. Root candidate is KV-cache eviction/timestamp math + an attention kernel that assumes contiguous kv layout. Repro is flaky but I was able to make it deterministic by forcing high seqlen, short kv capacity, and rapid alternation of input contexts.

Timeline (quick):
- 2026-03-01: first alert from staged e2e (repros rare, ~1/200 runs).
- 2026-03-04: added extra logging (--dump-kv-metrics) to canary images.
- 2026-03-06: reproduced locally by setting RED_KV_MAX_ENTRIES=512 and feeding two alternating 1800-token prompts.
- 2026-03-07: found kernel switch correlated with incident (fastkv_attn -> block_attn_v2).
- 2026-03-09: ran targeted bisect and confirmed forcing kernel to fastkv_attn removes duplication.

Repro steps I used (local dev VM):
1) build with debug symbols: bazel build //runtime:inference_binary --compilation_mode=dbg
2) start server: ./bazel-bin/runtime/inference_binary --bind=127.0.0.1:8080 --log-level=debug --dump-kv-metrics
3) env overrides: export RED_KV_MAX_ENTRIES=512; export RED_KV_EVICT_THRESH=0.7
4) sequence generator (Python, quick):
   for i in range(200):
       send_prompt("")  # alternating large prompts of ~1800 tokens
5) watch logs for lines with "KV_EVICT" and "ATTN_KERNEL_SWITCH"

Commands I ran (snippets):
$ RED_KV_MAX_ENTRIES=512 RED_KV_EVICT_THRESH=0.7 ./inference_binary --dump-kv -t 2>&1 | tee kv-debug.log
$ grep -n "KV_EVICT" kv-debug.log | sed -n '1,200p'
$ jq -r '.events[] | select(.type=="kv_event")' kv-metrics.json

Observed log patterns / excerpts: (redacted IDs)
[2026-03-06T14:12:23Z] KV_EVENT evict idx=409 last_write_ts=170 - evict_count=1
[2026-03-06T14:12:23Z] ATTN_KERNEL_SWITCH from=fastkv_attn to=block_attn_v2 reason=seqlen_threshold(2048)->3000
[2026-03-06T14:12:23Z] ASSERT kv_index < kv_ring_size FAILED (kv_index=513, kv_ring_size=512)
[2026-03-06T14:12:23Z] FALLBACK using kernel=compat_attn; request continued
[2026-03-06T14:12:24Z] MODEL_OUTPUT repeated_tokens=6 pattern="<start> ... <start>"

Notes on the ASSERT: it was thrown inside kv_ring.cc:read_entries_at_offset(), triggered by a computed index that equals max_entries (513). The eviction path says we just incremented tail and scheduled eviction of idx 1, so seeing 513 is suspicious (off-by-one / stale base offset).

Kernel selection behavior (what we saw):
- kernel selector uses heuristics: if seq_len > KERNEL_SWITCH_SEQLEN (2048 in config) -> choose block_attn_v2.
- block_attn_v2 expects contiguous slices of kv buffer (no modular wrap assumption) for vectorized gather. fastkv_attn supports modular ring layout with explicit offsets.
- At the exact moment of the switch we observed two things: evict_count > 0 and a concurrent writer that advanced head. The kernels may be reading different offset bases.

Experiments & results:
1) Force kernel: FASTKV only
   - cmd: ./inference_binary --force-attn-kernel=fastkv_attn ...
   - result: duplication disappeared across 3k runs. No ASSERT.
2) Reduce RED_KV_MAX_ENTRIES to 256
   - result: higher eviction churn, duplication rate increased (1/15 runs).
3) Increase RED_KV_MAX_ENTRIES to 8192
   - result: almost no duplication but sustained memory usage increased and latency tail got worse.
4) Add coarse-grained lock around eviction path (dev patch)
   - result: reduced race but added ~1.5ms median latency; duplication reduced but not eliminated.
5) Patch: clamp computed index modulo kv_ring_size before use
   - result: ASSERT gone, BUT model outputs still sometimes duplicated (suggests stale kv entries rather than index OOB only).

Hypotheses (ranked):
H1) Kernel assumption mismatch: block_attn_v2 assumes contiguous non-wrapping KV layout; when ring wraps while kernel selected, it reads stale data past boundary -> repeated tokens. Evidence: forcing fastkv_attn fixes it.
H2) Race between eviction and kernel selection: selector chooses block_attn_v2 based on observed seqlen; eviction then advances ring pointers while kernel uses prior base offset -> transient OOB. Evidence: eviction logs always present during incidents.
H3) Inconsistent timestamp semantics when computing eviction age: some writers use "last_write_ts" as monotonic ticks, others use system time; under heavy load these drift and cause premature evictions exposing invalid data. Evidence: mixed timestamp formats in logs from different threads.
H4) KV compaction bug: after many evicts the compaction routine leaves a small gap that block_attn_v2 misinterprets as valid contiguous region. Less evidence, lower priority.

Open questions / checks to run:
- Is block_attn_v2 actually implemented to handle modular offsets? I couldn't find an explicit modulo in gather_kernel.cc. Who owns that code? @Jon?
- Are there any memory fences around head/tail updates? I saw atomic stores but no explicit release semantics in the old code path. Need arch expert (Eleni) to confirm.
- Why did clamping indices remove ASSERT but not duplication? Are stale entries being populated with older KV values rather than being zeroed/invalidated?

Immediate next steps I plan:
1) Add explicit per-chunk version tag in KV entries (u64 generation id) and have kernels validate generation before use. Fast check: increment global generation on each eviction cycle. If kernel sees gen mismatch, fallback/retry. Low-risk but will add validation cost.
2) Instrument kernel selection path to log base_offset, kv_head, kv_tail, and generation id at switch time. Need to add structured log entries: {evt:ATTN_SWITCH, base_offset, head, tail, gen, seq_len}
3) Add unit test that simulates ring wrap with both kernels; run in stress for 30m.
4) Get SRE to run a canary with --force-attn-kernel=fastkv_attn to reduce incidents while we fix.
5) If H1 confirmed, document kernel contract and add guard that prevents block_attn_v2 selection when kv buffer is wrapping or when eviction_count>0.

Notes-to-self / fragments: 
- clip: read kernel gather implementation lines 142-190 for modulo behavior
- check PR#804 that rewrote eviction schedule (maybe introduced off-by-one)
- consider: stronger invariants (head % size != tail) not sufficient; need generation to disambiguate reused slots

Small debugging snippets I used to inspect memory: 
$ sudo perf record -p $(pidof inference_binary) -g -- sleep 4
$ sudo perf script | c++filt | sed -n '1,200p'
$ gdb -p $(pidof inference_binary) --batch -ex "call dump_kv_state()" -ex bt

Example dump_kv_state() output (sanitized):
KV_STATE: size=512 head=513 tail=1 gen=42 used=511 evict_in_progress=1
slots[510].gen=41 slots[511].gen=42 slots[0].gen=40

If you see head==size (513) that indicates we didn't wrap head back to 1 or we keep a monotonically increasing counter for head and rely on modulo elsewhere. That pattern is present. Need to ensure kernels use modulo at read time.

Potential quick patch (prototype, low-risk):
- Add kernel-side check: if base_offset >= kv_ring_size -> base_offset %= kv_ring_size (log once per 1000)
- Add gen check: if slot.gen != current_gen -> fallback to safe kernel or retry after fetch.

Longer-term: redesign KV API to return a contiguous view for kernels that need it (compaction / copy-on-read) but that has perf cost.

Callouts / TODOs:
- @Jon: please confirm whether block_attn_v2 was intentionally written to assume contiguous memory (no modulo).
- @Eleni: review atomic memory order semantics on head/tail updates in eviction code.
- @SRE: can we run the fastkv-only canary for 48h in eu-west-1? I'll prepare the safe flag and rollback plan.

References (local):
- runtime/src/kv/kv_ring.cc (eviction, compaction)
- runtime/src/attn/block_attn_v2/gather_kernel.cc
- runtime/logs/kv-debug-20260306.log (sanitized copy in the ticket)

Random thought: if block_attn_v2 is materially faster for long seqs but requires contiguous layout, maybe we should add a light-weight compaction step that only runs when seqlen crosses threshold and eviction_count==0. That would allow safe fast path without forcing everyone onto fastkv_attn.

End notes: this doc is messy — meant as a running breadcrumb trail. Will clean up if we escalate to a formal postmortem.

-- Maya
